newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen down on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen down on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell after a three-session 3.1-percent rise and analysts said the market could fall again on Tuesday, staying in its three-month flat trend amid conflicting signals.

Analysts said the current good macroecomic climate was countered by this year's heavy primary market and parliamentary elections due in September, though Bank Handlowy's final IPO issue price, due by Tuesday, could affect the market mood.
"A high price would show there's big interest in the share market and could have a psychological effect for a week or two," said Artur Kobos, a trader at ING Baring Securities.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.4 percent to 16,253.6 points and turnover eased 0.9 percent to 125.4 million zlotys ($38.7 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 53 to 28 with 24 stocks flat.

Analysts were surprised that profit-taking in National Investment Funds (NFIs) ensued as quickly as it did after the funds' NIF index's 6.4-percent Friday surge, saying speculation was dominating early fund trade, which started on Thursday.
The index closed at 169.4 points on Monday while the units rose 3.3 percent to 160 zlotys ($49.4).
Analysts said both the funds and units could fall on Tuesday after Monday's heavier selling of funds after price fixing and unit falls in continuous trade.

They said market sentiment could improve after the finance mininster's Monday statement inflation was 0.6 percent month on month and 14.6 percent year on year in May and another significant fall in year-on-year inflation was seen in June.
Analysts said some stocks saw illiquid price swings on Friday, such as builder KPBP Bick, down 9.8 percent. They were surprised by paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn's 9.8-percent fall.
